question_type: CPI-deflated monthly series (to a target month's dollars) followed by a 3-point OLS slope and intercept

opus_path.decision: Series = SB-4 'Unmatured > Total' column, calendar months Jan-Mar 1970, $ millions; deflator = CPI-U NSA 1982-84=100 with real_m = nominal_m * CPI_Mar / CPI_m; OLS of real value on month index, noting that the x coding (Jan=1 vs Jan=0) is ambiguous.
Table SB-4 'Redemptions of Matured and Unmatured Savings Bonds'. Cross-footed matured + unmatured + unclassified = total to rule out a column shift.
Vintage loop 1970_03..1972_06: identical in every issue that prints the rows, so vintage is moot. There was one dead end: the loop first keyed on an SB-2 table and was re-keyed on the title.
Confirmed there is no monthly CPI-U table in the corpus, so CPI comes from external knowledge.
EXTERNAL KNOWLEDGE: CPI-U NSA (CUUR0000SA0) Jan-Mar 1970, anchored against neighbours (Dec 1969, Apr 1970) and the 1970 annual average.
Deflated to March dollars and ran OLS with x=1,2,3 (also reported x=0,1,2 as an alternative), in a script.
Slope equals (y3-y1)/2 for three equally spaced points; magnitude matches the calendar-1969 monthly average. Reviewer re-read cells and recomputed independently.

right_arms_note: No arm was right. All three arms produced the same wrong answer from the same wrong recalled Jan-Mar 1970 CPI values. Everything else (table, cells, deflation direction, x=1..3, rounding) matched Opus.
text_vs_mechanism: Text alone cannot fix this: the prompt arm already carried a lesson saying never to fill CPI values from memory and had no alternative source, so it recalled them anyway. The failure is missing external data, so it needs a TOOL (vetted CPI reference series) or equivalent grounded STATE, not more instructions.
notes: (1) The CPI recall error is systematic, not random: all three independent arms recalled identical Jan-Mar 1970 values but different Apr-Dec values. A self-consistency or majority-vote CONTROL over multiple recalls would NOT have caught it. Only external reference data would. (2) This is a clean case for measuring the value of a reference-data tool: with correct CPI inputs, all three arms' existing computations would reproduce Opus. (3) The prompt arm's 'latest printing' hunt ([13]-[48]) was driven by a lesson about a different table family (SBN). Scope-mismatched vintage lessons cost time even when harmless; a STATE index of 'series X is vintage-stable in years Y' would let the actor skip it.
